question: I got a parking ticket yesterday because my permit was still processing. how do I appeal it and who do I email
answer:
Public Safety says an owner/driver must appeal within 20 days of the citation’s issuance; filing late forfeits the right to appeal [1][2]. The pages give different submission instructions: section 1 says appeals are accepted at citation@ramapo.edu; sections 2 and 10 say to appeal online, through the appeal portal: https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3 [1][2][10]. The pages differ on how to submit; to cover both instructions, use the portal and email citation@ramapo.edu. Identify the specific ground(s) for appeal and briefly explain your justification [1]. Section 10 also says to provide supporting evidence, such as witness statements or photographs [10]. The listed reasons not considered include ignorance of regulations and disagreement with the rules; the pages do not say whether a permit still processing is an accepted appeal ground [1][2][10].
For a question about your permit processing, email parkingpermits@ramapo.edu and include your Ramapo student ID # (R#) [4]. Citations not paid or appealed within 20 days are subject to a $5 late fee [3].

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/vehicle-citation-information/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/how-to-apply-for-a-parking-permit/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/)

question: refund
answer:
For credit-balance refunds, Student Accounts says a Title IV aid overpayment with a credit balance of $1.00 or greater will be refunded; non-Title IV aid credit balances have a $5.00 threshold. Unless you specify otherwise, the College issues a paper check, mailed to your billing/permanent address. Checks are not mailed to campus mailboxes and cannot be picked up at Student Accounts. [1]

For a fall-term refund, you may ask to have proceeds applied to spring by emailing studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Spring proceeds cannot be applied to the following fall. Electronic/direct deposit is free. [1]

To set it up: [6]
1. “Log into RCNJ Experience” and locate the “Student Account Info” card.
2. Click “Bill & Payment Suite,” then “Electronic Refunds” under “My Profile Setup.”
3. Enroll in Two-Step Verification (skip if already completed): in “Security Settings,” select a passcode method, click “Send Code,” enter the passcode, then “Verify.”
4. In “Payment Profile,” edit or create a payment method and check the box in “Refund Option” to designate it for direct deposit.

For withdrawal-related refunds, students who officially drop or withdraw from courses and/or housing, following the Registrar and/or Residence Life policies, procedures, and deadlines, may be eligible for account adjustments. After College refund deadlines, withdrawals are not eligible for refunds or account adjustments. Housing deposits are non-refundable. Contact the Office of the Registrar for help with a withdrawal: https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/. [5]

Student Accounts: studentaccts@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7495, D-Wing, First Floor. [1]

question: How do I set up a payment plan for spring semester tuition? and is there a fee to enroll in it
answer:
For Spring 2027, Student Accounts offers a four- or five-month Ramapo Tuition Payment Plan (RTPP), beginning November 16, 2026. Enroll online by logging into [RCNJ Experience](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/) before the semester’s posted payment deadline. Pay the down payment and setup fee when you enroll. The five-month plan requires 20% down; the four-month plan requires 25%. [1]

Spring installments are scheduled December–April for the five-month plan, or January–April for the four-month plan. Additional payments are due on the 15th of each month after enrollment. [1, 3, 5] The plan has no interest. There is a non-refundable $60 setup fee, also described as a $60 service fee. [1, 2]

Past-due balances from previous semesters of $500 or more must be paid before you’re eligible; the College may deny enrollment based on past payment history. Enrolling after the down-payment due date requires paying missed installments at enrollment. Missing the payment deadline may result in a $200 late fee and/or deregistration. [1]

Questions: Student Accounts, (201) 684-7495 or studentaccts@ramapo.edu. [1]

question: how do I get credit for my internship? I need to register for it but dont know where to start
answer:
Start with the Cahill Career Development Center. Co-op is an academic course, and you request permission to register. After you’re accepted for an internship: [1]
1. Select and meet with a co-op faculty advisor to determine your learning objectives and academic assignment. [1]
2. Request a “(co-op) Experience” on Handshake, then meet with your career advisor. [1]
3. Get “Registration Permission” from the Career Center. Permission lets you take the course; it is not registration. [1]
4. If choosing Pass/Fail, complete the appropriate form with Academic Advisement. If you are an international student on a J1 or other visa, get authorization from the international advisor and complete the appropriate paperwork. [1]
5. Register through “Self Service” on “My Ramapo.” [1]

Complete a Learning Agreement approved by your faculty advisor, career advisor, and employment supervisor. [9] An internship must provide meaningful work related to your major and/or career objective, building on classroom or academic experience. [3] Co-op is available in fall, spring, and summer. The published hour minimums are 120 hours in a semester for 2 credits or 240 hours for 4 credits. [2]

The pages differ on credits: section 2 lists 2- or 4-credit options; section 9 says each successfully completed co-op course is 4 credits. The pages also differ on orientation: section 4 requires first-time students to attend one orientation and all students to attend reflection; section 9 says students must attend both. [2][4][9]

Contact the Cahill Career Development Center: careercenter@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7444 (Main Office, C-209) or (201) 684-7675 (ASB Office, ASB-513). [1]

question: What do I need to do to move out of my dorm when I graduate? is there a checkout process and what happens if I'm late
answer:
Housing & Residence Life’s published end-of-spring checkout guidance says to follow the checklist before leaving. Remove trash and recyclables; leave the College refrigerator on at level 5; remove personal items; set the thermostat to auto, low, at 70°F; clean your room; close blinds, lock windows, turn off lights, close the door, empty your campus mailbox, update correspondents with your new mailing address, and leave drawers open. Leave by your checkout deadline, based on your last exam schedule. [1] All students must review and follow the checklist: https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/check-out-checklist/ [2]

If you need to stay past the designated checkout date and time, complete the Check-Out Extension Request process: https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/. Extensions are not granted for non-academic reasons, including unavailable/late transportation and off-campus employment. Approved extensions do not allow guests. [6]

Not vacating as required or failing to abide by posted checkout times may result in a $75 improper-checkout fine. Excessive garbage is $25 per bag; damage charges are determined case by case. [2][4] Final inspections occur after halls and apartments are vacated; failed inspections or prohibited items may be billed, and items left behind are discarded. [9] Damage, missing College property, or policy violations may also result in a post-checkout billing notice by email. [7]

These pages don’t give a graduation-specific checkout date or separate graduate process. Ask your RA or Hall office before checkout. For help, contact Housing & Residence Life at reslife@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7461. [1]

question: My RA wrote me up for a candle. what happens now? do i have to go to a hearing
answer:
A candle is a prohibited item, and Residence Life staff address prohibited-item violations. [9] The Office of Student Conduct receives incident reports from Residence Life staff and other sources. [18] Check your college email daily; conduct communications are sent there, and missing a message is not an excuse for missing a hearing or deadline. [21]

The pages don’t say that every candle write-up requires a hearing, so I can’t verify whether you personally have to attend one. If the Office schedules a hearing, the page describes it as an opportunity to talk about what happened; trying to avoid responsibility may lead to more severe sanctions. [5] Contact the Office of Student Conduct with questions about your case. [13, 21] You may have an advisor of your choosing, including an attorney, present, but the advisor may not speak during the hearing. [1]

The listed consequences depend on what violation is charged and whether it is a first or later offense. For “Activating a fire alarm due to a disregard of a published policy,” with candles as an example, the first violation is a $150 fine and fire-safety reflection assignment; the second is a $300 fine, disciplinary probation, and possible suspension or loss of housing privileges. [4] These are for activating a fire alarm—not necessarily for possession of a candle alone. [4, 6]

Office of Student Conduct: studentconduct@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7869, C-212. [1, 21]

question: how do i get a parking permit and how much does it cost
answer:
**How to apply:** Public Safety directs students to the online Parking Permit Registration portal [6, 9]. Its regulations say to ensure the parking fee is on your RCNJ student account, then visit the Parking Permits webpage [7]. Another page gives these steps: “Enter Permit Type and click Continue”; complete Contact Information, click “Save/Update Person” and “Continue”; enter Vehicle Information and “Continue”; review and “Continue”; then print or save the Registration Filed page as verification—not as the permit. Select the correct housing assignment or commuter status, and “student,” not “faculty/staff” [12].

The Orientation FAQ gives a different portal and process: log on to ThePermitStore.com; enter Ramapo as your destination, choose Ramapo College of New Jersey, click Apply, agree to terms, sign in, complete the four application steps (personal information, permit, vehicle, payment), then Finish. It says to print the temporary permit, display it on the dashboard until the permanent permit arrives, then activate the permit online [11]. The pages therefore give different portal instructions [6, 9, 11, 12].

New students pick up permits at New Student Check-In; returning residents at their on-campus mailbox; returning commuters at the Public Safety ID Office during weekday operating hours, or at the Main Desk after 3 pm by emailing to request another pickup time [7, 12]. Permit fee automatically appears on the term bill [1, 10]. Applications open mid-May for summer permits and early August for Fall/Spring permits; follow Public Safety messages for specific dates [10].

**Cost:** The 2026–2027 fee text includes “Spring-only Commuter Parking Tax Charge | $8.29,” “Spring-only Resident Parking Supplement | $25.00,” “Summer-only Parking Permit | $100.00,” and “Summer-only Commuter Parking Tax Charge | $6.63” [5]. It also has the truncated fragment “student) | $125.00,” which does not identify the charge [5]. Off-campus students are charged 6.63% NJ sales tax on parking fees; on-campus students are exempt [1]. The regular permit price is not clear in the provided fee text [5].

For questions, Public Safety: parkingpermits@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7432; include your Ramapo student ID number (R#) in an email [8, 12].

question: im a transfer student and i commute, how do i get a parking permit and where do i park
answer:
**Public Safety** handles permits and parking. Register at [Parking Permits](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/) [2, 3].

One page’s steps: “Enter Permit Type and click Continue”; complete Contact Information, click “Save/Update Person” and “Continue”; enter Vehicle Information and click “Continue”; review the request and click “Continue”; print or save the “Registration Filed” page with your request number. That page is verification, not the permit. Select “student” and the correct commuter status. New-student permits are available for pickup during New Student Check-In. [9]

The pages differ: another student FAQ instead directs applicants to https://ramapo.thepermitstore.com/ and gives a different process: enter Ramapo, choose Ramapo College of New Jersey, click Apply, agree to terms, sign in; complete personal information, select a permit, enter vehicle information, proceed to payment (dropdown should read “No Payment Necessary”), then Finish. It says to print a temporary permit from the account, display it until the permanent permit arrives by mail, then activate the permit online. [10]

For 2026–2027, the listed Fall/Spring permit is $250.00 and the Fall/Spring Commuter Parking Tax Charge is $16.58. Off-campus students are subject to 6.63% sales tax. [14, 11]

**Where to park:** The page says students may use C1, C2, or D lots as overflow if their assigned lot is full. It does not identify your assigned commuter lot. Commuters may not park overnight (2am–6am) without prior Public Safety authorization. [5]

For your assigned lot or which application process applies, contact Public Safety at parkingpermits@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7432. [9, 21]

question: do transfer students need to take all the gen ed / Intellectual Inquiry requirements again or do some get waived?
answer:
No—not necessarily. Transfer students may transfer in or be waived from some or all General Education requirements [3].

• NJ community college graduates with an A.A. or A.S. are waived from General Education requirements after submitting a final official transcript with the conferred degree. A.A.S. graduates are not eligible for a full waiver; courses are evaluated individually [8].
• Students transferring at least 48 credits from an accredited institution without a completed A.A. or A.S. degree are waived from some requirements [2]. For students with at least 48 credits, the listed waived keystone courses are First Year Seminar, Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Social Science Inquiry, and Studies in the Arts and Humanities. They must still fulfill Critical Reading and Writing 102, Quantitative Reasoning, and Scientific Reasoning, and take one course from two of Culture and Creativity, Values and Ethics, and Social Systems and Society [1].
• Transfer credits are generally considered for possible Gen Ed waivers only if accepted in the semester of matriculation [4]. The distribution requirement is two of those three categories [7].

Catalog transfer-equivalent courses listed are: HIST 100T TRANSFER GE HISTORY EQUIVALENT: Gen Ed 18-Historical Prspctve (GEHP); INTD 200T TRANSFER GE GLOBA AWR EQ: Gen Ed 18-Global Awareness (GEGA); INTD 201T TRANSFER GE CULT & CREAT EQ: Gen Ed 18-Culture & Creativity (GECC); INTD 203T TRANSFER GE VAL & ETH EQ: Gen Ed 18-Values and Ethics (GEVE); and INTD 280 TRANSFER ELECTIVE: VALUE & ETHICS: Gen Ed 18-Values and Ethics (GEVE). EDUC 211 STUDENT LITERACY CORPS: Gen Ed 18-Values and Ethics (GEVE) [11].

Office of the Provost can advise you on applicable waivers and remaining requirements during academic advisement [1]. Email provost@ramapo.edu or call (201) 684-7330. Admissions: admissions@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7300 [8].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#waiver-of-general-education-requirements1) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#waiver-of-general-education-requirements1) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#transferring-academic-credit1) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/admission-requirements/) [11](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: how do i find out why my financial aid hasnt shown up yet and who do i talk to
answer:
Check the Account Summary screen for pending (estimated or anticipated) aid and authorized aid, which appear in separate sections. For more detail, click the Student Accounts page’s “here” link, then click “Billing and Financial Aid Terminology.” [1][2]

Authorized aid has met all requirements for payment and is credited on the official term disbursement date, typically four weeks into a term. “Memos” are pending aid transactions needing further action, except New Jersey Class Loans, Alternative Loans, and Outside Scholarships; those are credited when the funding agency pays. For all other aid shown as a Memo, the page strongly recommends contacting the Office of Financial Aid to resolve outstanding issues. [2]

Contact the Office of Financial Aid: email finaid@ramapo.edu or call (201) 684-7549. It is in E-210 (Academic Building). You can request an in-person appointment by email or through the chat on its website; appointments are Monday through Friday, 8:30am to 4:30pm. The office says most questions can also be handled by phone, Webex, or email. [5][7]
